---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5. CI tests all three.
- The `mbstring` and `tokenizer` PHP extensions. Most PHP builds include both.
  juphyter 0.1.1 and later declare both in composer.json, so Composer reports
  a missing one at install time.
- Composer.
- Python 3 with the `venv` module. On Debian and Ubuntu that module is the
  `python3-venv` package.
- macOS or Linux.

Optional:

- The `pcntl` PHP extension makes the stop button interrupt a running cell.
  Without it the kernel runs and the stop button does nothing.
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) renders `.qmd` documents. CI
  tests Quarto 1.10.18.
- The [vl-convert](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases) binary gives
  phiz plots a static image for PDF and Word output.
  [Quarto](quarto.qmd#what-each-format-carries) covers when it is needed.

juphyter does not use the `posix` or `sockets` PHP extensions.

The kernel runs inside a Python environment that has
[ipykernel](https://pypi.org/project/ipykernel/) 7.0 or later.
`juphyter install` uses an existing environment that has it, or builds one
with JupyterLab in it. ipykernel 7.4, the current release, requires Python
3.11 or later. The commands below were run on 2026-10-31 with juphyter 0.1.0,
on macOS with Python 3.14 and on Debian 13 with Python 3.13.

## Install

Install juphyter once for your user. A kernel is registered for the user, so
one install serves notebooks and documents in every directory.

```bash
composer global require phpstats/juphyter
export PATH="$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):$PATH"
juphyter install --create-venv ~/.venvs/juphyter
export PATH="$HOME/.venvs/juphyter/bin:$PATH"
juphyter doctor
```

The commands do the following:

1. `composer global require` installs juphyter into Composer's global
   directory.
2. The first `export` puts Composer's bin directory on `PATH` for this
   shell, so the `juphyter` command is found.
3. `juphyter install` registers the kernel with Jupyter under the name `php`.
   It uses the Python environment that owns the `jupyter` command on `PATH`
   when that environment has ipykernel. Otherwise it builds a virtual
   environment with JupyterLab at the path `--create-venv` names, using the
   Python already on the machine. It changes no existing Python
   installation.
4. The second `export` puts that environment first on `PATH` for this shell,
   so `jupyter lab` and `quarto render` find it. When step 3 used an existing
   environment, the directory does not exist and the line has no effect.
5. `juphyter doctor` checks the installation. It changes nothing.

Both `export` lines last until the shell closes.

`juphyter install` prints what it registered:

```
Installed the juphyter kernel "php" for PHP 8.5.10.
  kernel.json  /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php/kernel.json
  python       /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python (ipykernel 7.4.0)
  php          /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php/8.5.10/bin/php
  engine       /Users/you/.composer/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/bin/juphyter
  quarto       /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14 (no Jupyter)
```

The `quarto` line names the Python that Quarto would use from this shell. It
appears only when Quarto is installed. Here it was printed before the second
`export`, so it names a Python without Jupyter, and the command also printed
a warning with the `export` line that fixes it. The kernel is still
registered, and the command exits 0.

On Homebrew, juphyter 0.1.0 recorded the versioned path under `Cellar` shown
above, which `brew upgrade` removes. juphyter 0.1.1 and later record the first
path on `PATH` with the same name that leads to the running PHP, such as
`/opt/homebrew/bin/php`. With 0.1.0, pass that path explicitly:

```bash
juphyter install --php /opt/homebrew/bin/php
```

### Keeping the PATH entries

To keep the `juphyter` command available in new shells, add Composer's bin
directory to your shell startup file. This edits `~/.zshrc`, the zsh startup
file. Use `~/.bashrc` for bash.

```bash
echo "export PATH=\"$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):\$PATH\"" >> ~/.zshrc
```

Adding the Python environment to a startup file makes it the `python3` for
every program in every shell, including every Quarto project on the machine.
[Python interpreters and editors](python.qmd) describes how to select it per
editor workspace, per shell, or per Quarto project instead.

## Check the installation

```bash
juphyter doctor
```

`juphyter doctor` checks juphyter's own files, the PHP that runs the cells,
the Python for the kernel, the Python Quarto will use, and every kernel
juphyter registered. It ends with one line for JupyterLab and one for
Quarto. After the install above:

```
juphyter doctor

This package
  ok    the Python wrapper is at /Users/you/.composer/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/kernel/juphyter_kernel

PHP
  ok    PHP 8.5.10 at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php/8.5.10/bin/php
  ok    pcntl is there, so the stop button interrupts a cell

A Python for the kernel
  ok    /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python has ipykernel 7.4.0

Quarto
  ok    quarto will run /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python3, with jupyter_client 8.10.0

Kernels in /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels
  ok    php is complete

JupyterLab: ready, with php.
Quarto: ready.
```

A line marked `fail` makes the command exit 1. A line marked `warn` does not.
A missing `pcntl` is a warning.

In a shell where the Python environment is not on `PATH`, the Quarto section
fails, the summary reads `Quarto: not ready.`, and the report ends with the
`export` line that fixes it. JupyterLab still works if you start it from the
environment, for example `~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab`.

Run `juphyter doctor` again after upgrading PHP or Python, or after removing a
project or an environment. The kernel records absolute paths to a PHP binary,
a Python interpreter, and juphyter itself, and the doctor reports any of them
that no longer runs.

## The phpstats packages

juphyter does not depend on phibble, phplyr, or phiz. To use them in
notebooks outside any Composer project, install them globally and register a
second kernel that loads Composer's global autoloader:

```bash
composer global require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
juphyter install --name phpstats --display-name "PHP (phpstats)" \
  --autoload "$(composer global config home)/vendor/autoload.php"
```

Documents name that kernel as `jupyter: phpstats`, and JupyterLab lists it as
"PHP (phpstats)".

The `php` kernel keeps the default search for an autoloader, described below.
A kernel installed with `--autoload` always loads the autoloader it names,
even for a notebook inside a Composer project, which is why it has its own
name.

## Which classes a notebook sees

By default the kernel starts in the notebook's directory, looks upward for
`vendor/autoload.php`, and loads the first one it finds. A notebook anywhere
inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages with no
configuration.

Two settings replace that search. The more explicit one wins.

1. `JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD` in the kernel's environment. `juphyter install
   --autoload PATH` records it in the kernel.
2. A `juphyter.json` in the notebook's directory or any directory above it.

A `juphyter.json` can also set the memory limit and the include path:

```json
{
  "autoload": "vendor/autoload.php",
  "memory_limit": "512M",
  "include_path": "lib"
}
```

Relative paths resolve against the directory that holds `juphyter.json`, so
one file at a project's root serves every notebook below it.

## Installing into one project

juphyter can also be a development dependency of a project:

```bash
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name myproject
```

The kernel is still registered for your user, and it runs that project's copy
of juphyter. Without `--name`, a second project's install replaces the first
project's `php` kernel, and the command reports it as `Replaced`. Deleting the
project's `vendor` directory breaks the kernel, which `juphyter doctor`
reports.

## Several PHP versions

Give each kernel its own name:

```bash
juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php
juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php
```

JupyterLab then lists "PHP 8.3" and "PHP 8.5". `--display-name` sets the label
yourself. An absolute `--php` path is recorded as written. A bare name such as
`php8.4` is resolved to an absolute path, because a kernel cannot rely on
`PATH`.

## Where the kernel is registered

`juphyter install` writes a kernelspec, the `kernel.json` file Jupyter reads
to start a kernel, into the per-user Jupyter data directory:

- `~/Library/Jupyter/kernels` on macOS.
- `$XDG_DATA_HOME/jupyter/kernels`, or `~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels`, on
  Linux.

It honors `JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` and `JUPYTER_PLATFORM_DIRS` as `jupyter --paths`
reports them. `--prefix PATH` writes under `PATH/share/jupyter` instead. Every
Jupyter installation on the machine searches the per-user directory, so the
kernel is visible to all of them.

`juphyter uninstall --name NAME` removes a kernel that juphyter registered. It
refuses to remove a kernel of the same name that something else wrote, and so
does a reinstall.

## Options

`juphyter install --help` lists every option:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--name NAME` | The kernel's name, which documents use in `jupyter: NAME`. Default: `php`. |
| `--display-name TEXT` | The label JupyterLab shows. Default: the PHP version, such as `PHP 8.5`. |
| `--php PATH` | The PHP binary that runs cells. Default: the PHP running `juphyter install`. |
| `--python PATH` | The Python that hosts the kernel. Default: the one that owns `jupyter` on `PATH`. A named Python without ipykernel is reported, and nothing is installed into it. |
| `--prefix PATH` | Write under `PATH/share/jupyter`. |
| `--autoload PATH` | Load this autoloader instead of searching above the notebook. |
| `--create-venv PATH` | Where to build a Python environment when none can host the kernel. Without it, the command asks, and builds one at `~/.venvs/juphyter` when there is no terminal to ask. |

`juphyter --version` prints the installed version and the PHP running it.
